\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Norm of a Rademacher sum]
\lean{FABL.rademacherNorm}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p066-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p115-b002
}
\label{FABL.rademacherNorm}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.signValue}
Let $V$ be a real normed vector space, let $w_1,\ldots,w_n\in V$, and let
$x=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\in\{-1,1\}^n$. The Rademacher norm of $w$ at $x$ is the norm of
$\sum_{i=1}^n \operatorname{signValue}(x_i)w_i$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Weighted sum after a coordinate flip]
\lean{FABL.signedSum_flipCoordinate}
\label{FABL.signedSum_flipCoordinate}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.flipCoordinate, FABL.setCoordinate, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n\ge 0$, let $V$ be a real normed vector space, let $w_0,\ldots,w_{n-1}\in V$, let
$x\in\{-1,1\}^n$, and choose a coordinate $i$. The weighted sum of the signs after
flipping coordinate $i$ equals the original weighted sum minus twice the contribution
from coordinate $i$; that is, $\sum_j x'_j w_j=\sum_j x_jw_j-2x_iw_i$, where $x'$ agrees
with $x$ except that $x'_i=-x_i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Coordinate flip sum identity]
\lean{FABL.sum_signedSum_flipCoordinate}
\label{FABL.sum_signedSum_flipCoordinate}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.flipCoordinate, FABL.signValue, FABL.signedSum_flipCoordinate}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $V$ be a real normed vector space, let
$w_1,\ldots,w_n\in V$, and let $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$. For each coordinate $i$, form the point
obtained by flipping coordinate $i$ of $x$. The sum over all $i$ of the signed vector
sums at these flipped points equals $(n-2)$ times the signed vector sum at $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Vanishing for even functions and odd sets]
\lean{FABL.fourierCoeff_eq_zero_of_even_of_odd_card}
\label{FABL.fourierCoeff_eq_zero_of_even_of_odd_card}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.monomial, FABL.monomial_neg_input}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n\ge 0$, let $f$ be a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
satisfying $f(-x)=f(x)$ for every input $x$, and let $S$ be a coordinate set of odd
cardinality. Then the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $S$ is zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Variance bounded by total influence]
\lean{FABL.two_mul_variance_le_totalInfluence_of_even}
\label{FABL.two_mul_variance_le_totalInfluence_of_even}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.fourierCoeff_eq_zero_of_even_of_odd_card, FABL.totalInfluence, FABL.totalInfluence_eq_sum_card_mul_sq_fourierCoeff, FABL.variance, FABL.variance_eq_sum_sq_fourierCoeff}
\difficulty{5}
Let $f:\{-1,1\} \to \mathbb R$ be an even function on the
sign cube of dimension $n$. Then twice the variance of $f$ is at most its total
influence.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Evenness of the Rademacher norm]
\lean{FABL.rademacherNorm_even}
\label{FABL.rademacherNorm_even}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.rademacherNorm, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{4}
Let $V$ be a real normed vector space and let $w_1,\ldots,w_n\in V$. The function on
sign vectors defined by $x\mapsto\left\|\sum_{i=1}^n x_i w_i\right\|$ is even: its
value at $-x$ equals its value at $x$ for every sign vector $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Laplacian bound for a Rademacher norm]
\lean{FABL.laplacian_rademacherNorm_le}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p066-b003}
\label{FABL.laplacian_rademacherNorm_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.flipCoordinate, FABL.laplacian, FABL.laplacian_eq_sum_sub_flip_div_two, FABL.rademacherNorm, FABL.signValue, FABL.sum_signedSum_flipCoordinate}
\difficulty{4}
Let $V$ be a real normed vector space, let $w_1,\ldots,w_n\in V$, and let
$x\in\{-1,1\}^n$. For the function $y\mapsto\left\|\sum_{i=1}^n y_iw_i\right\|$, its
Laplacian at $x$ is at most $\left\|\sum_{i=1}^n x_iw_i\right\|$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Two-coordinate Rademacher norm]
\lean{FABL.rademacherNorm_two_equal_weights}
\label{FABL.rademacherNorm_two_equal_weights}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.monomial, FABL.rademacherNorm, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{4}
For every pair of signs $x_1,x_2\in\{-1,1\}$, the Euclidean norm of their sum satisfies
$|x_1+x_2|=1+x_1x_2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Moments of a two-coordinate Rademacher norm]
\lean{FABL.rademacherNorm_two_equal_weights_moments}
\label{FABL.rademacherNorm_two_equal_weights_moments}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.expect_monomial, FABL.monomial, FABL.monomial_sq, FABL.rademacherNorm, FABL.rademacherNorm_two_equal_weights}
\difficulty{4}
For a uniformly random sign vector $x=(x_1,x_2)\in\{-1,1\}^2$, the norm of the sum of
its coordinates has first moment $1$ and second moment $2$: $\mathbb{E}|x_1+x_2|=1$ and
$\mathbb{E}|x_1+x_2|^2=2$.
\end{theorem}
